response.answer: Contested-denial audits need uninterrupted review because switching to routine queue messages can break the chronology needed to interpret evidence correctly. In one water-damage audit, interruptions led to treating a later repair estimate as pre-dating a policy lapse and incorrectly upholding a denial. A protected hour preserves focus for appeal-risk decisions, while a queue coordinator can hold routine questions and send a summary afterward so the queue still moves. Only urgent or legally significant matters—such as vulnerable-customer escalations, regulator requests, or data-security issues—should interrupt.
